questions.q: How does the Terraform CLI itself get installed on Windows?
options: It only runs inside a Docker container and cannot be installed as a standalone binary
It requires a full HashiCorp Cloud Platform subscription before the CLI will run locally
It is bundled inside every provider plugin and installs automatically with the first provider you add
As a self-contained binary, via winget/choco or a manual download from releases.hashicorp.com — no separate runtime required
questions.explain: Terraform ships as a single self-contained binary; winget install HashiCorp.Terraform or choco install terraform puts terraform.exe on your PATH, and terraform version confirms the install.

questions.q: Which of the following does Terraform's core engine actually know how to do, according to this lesson?
options: Make authenticated REST calls directly to the Azure Resource Manager API without any provider plugin
Compile Bicep files down to ARM JSON
Parse HCL, build a dependency graph of declared resources, diff desired config against state, and produce a plan
Automatically detect which cloud provider's API a resource block is meant for, without a required_providers block
questions.explain: Terraform core is cloud-agnostic — it only handles generic HCL parsing, graph building, state diffing, and plan generation. Talking to a specific cloud's API is a provider's job.

questions.q: What is a Terraform provider, such as hashicorp/azurerm?
options: A separately versioned plugin that translates Terraform's generic actions into real API calls against one specific system
A YAML file that lists every resource in your Azure subscription
A built-in feature of Terraform core that ships inside the terraform.exe binary itself
A replacement for the terraform CLI used only on Linux
questions.explain: Providers are plugins, built and versioned independently of Terraform core, each one knowing how to talk to one specific cloud or system's API.

questions.q: In a required_providers block, what does the `source` field do?
options: Specifies the file path to a local .tf file on disk
Lists the resource group the provider is allowed to modify
Sets the Azure region the provider will deploy resources into
Names the publisher and provider on the Terraform Registry, e.g. "hashicorp/azurerm"
questions.explain: source = "hashicorp/azurerm" tells Terraform exactly which provider to download from the Terraform Registry — hashicorp is the publisher, azurerm is the provider name.

questions.q: Why does a required_providers block typically include a version constraint like `version = "~> 3.100"`?
options: Version constraints are only cosmetic and have no effect on which provider release is downloaded
To set the version of Azure Resource Manager the subscription is running
Because Terraform refuses to run at all without an exact version pin on every provider
To pin the provider to an acceptable version range so an unexpected major-version upgrade can't silently change behavior
questions.explain: The version constraint controls which provider releases terraform init is allowed to download, protecting a configuration from breaking changes in an unconstrained upgrade.
